Google\'s picker hands out photos without their location data and videos as re-encoded copies, not the originals you uploaded. Every pulled file is labelled accordingly. Full-fidelity export via Google Takeout is planned for a later version.

Pomegranate shows you, for every photo and video, whether it is on this phone, in Google Photos, or both. Then it pulls everything that only exists in the cloud into a folder you choose, proves each copy, and lets you leave Google Photos cleanly.
Everything happens on this phone. The only servers ever contacted are Google\'s sign-in and Photos Picker, and only when you ask.

Everything stays on this phone: a list of your device photos and videos (names, sizes, dates, dimensions), the Google Photos items you picked, how they match, transfer records with file hashes, your settings, and an encrypted Google sign-in that is wiped on Disconnect. Nothing is sent anywhere except to Google, and only when you connect or pull.

Pomegranate shows where each photo lives (this phone, Google Photos, or both), copies what is only in the cloud into a folder you choose, proves each copy with a hash, and then cuts its own access to Google so you can leave cleanly. It never deletes anything.

No data leaves this phone except requests to Google\'s sign-in and Photos Picker services, made only when you ask. There are no analytics, no crash reporting and no third-party services. Your Google access is revoked and all related data deleted when you disconnect.

Your destination is inside a folder Google Photos usually backs up. Turn off backup for it (steps below) before deleting anything, or your copies may be uploaded again.
Tick the box above to unlock these steps.
Open the Google Photos app on this phone or photos.google.com on a computer.
Open Library, or search for a month or album you have verified.
Long-press one item, then drag or tap to select the rest. On a computer, click the first item, hold Shift and click the last.
Tap Delete (the bin) and confirm. Items go to Trash for 60 days.
To free the space now: Library → Trash → Empty trash.
In Google Photos, tap your profile picture → Photos settings.
Tap Backup and switch it off.
Alternatively keep backup on but open "Back up device folders" and switch off the folders you do not want uploaded, including your Pomegranate destination.
On a computer, also sign out of or uninstall any Google Photos uploader (such as Drive for desktop).
Turning off backup stops new uploads; it does not delete what is already there.
